Wave-staggered kinetic list

I wanted to know if one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas could drive independent staggered harmonic springs across five live drawable HTML list rows, shearing each card and splitting R/B chroma trails as you filter, shuffle or flick-scroll. Filter the list, drag vertically to flick, or tap Pin and +1 on any settled row.

Show the code five drawable rows, 48 ms spring wave, skew + chroma shader, hit-box sync and 2D fallback
  1. Five live drawable row cards inside one canvas. Each row keeps its category badge, counter text, Pin toggle and +1 button inside #ks-canvas.
  2. Deterministic tMs harmonic springs with 48 ms stagger. stepRowSprings(rows, tMs) runs 240 Hz symplectic substeps, holds pre-launch elastic tension during each row's i * 48 ms delay and settles cleanly to 1:1.
  3. Padded-quad velocity shear and R/B chroma split. STAGGER_FRAG shears each row by uSkew, runs 16-tap mipmapped vertical directional blur and splits R/B channels proportional to velocity before snapping to direct texel copy at rest.
  4. Hit-test sync across shuffled and filtered rows. syncRowGeometry() scales updateElementGeometry() by cached geometryUnit(), toggles data-hit-tick and sets inert plus an offstage matrix on filtered-out rows.
  5. Five-argument 2D and plain-HTML fallbacks. Draws skewed rows with 5-argument drawElementImage() when WebGL 2 is absent, and moves rows into #plain-host on context loss or without the API.

How it works

  • One ElementGL WebGL 2 context manages all five drawable rows inside #ks-canvas. Each row lays out at left: 0; top: 0 with an explicit responsive width and height derived from canvas.clientWidth.
  • Inside paint, once hasPainted is true and stage.begin() sizes the drawing buffer, dirty rows upload via gl.texElementSubImage2D() with UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL = true and generate texture mipmaps so fast vertical blur stays free of text ringing.
  • When you click Shuffle order, switch filter tabs, type in the filter box or flick-scroll the viewport, each row targets its new slot index with a 48 ms stagger offset per slot. stepRowSprings(rows, tMs) outputs per-row posY, skewX, blurPx and chromaPx from velocity.
  • Each row renders on a quad padded by 48 px horizontally and 36 px vertically so sheared corners and R/B chromatic trails never clip at card edges. At rest, the shader takes a 1:1 passthrough branch.
  • syncRowGeometry() writes calibrated updateElementGeometry() transforms for every visible row, toggles data-hit-tick to clear Chromium's hit-test cache, and marks filtered-out or offscreen rows inert with an offstage matrix.

Each check builds an isolated fixture inside the hidden test stage and retires its canvas when done. The list above isn't touched.

Findings

Measured in headless Chrome 160.0.8188.0 canary on 2026-11-27 (412 px phone viewport at 2.625 DPR and 1024 px desktop): 6/6 live checks pass on one ElementGL WebGL 2 context (937x941 px, 0.88 MP, 7.05 MB, 0 lost contexts, 0 open snapshots, 0 unasked readbacks). Tap "Run these 6 checks" above to measure your browser.

  • Not verified yet: real GPU frame rates, touch flick responsiveness and Android Chrome 159 behaviour at 412 px wide, plus Playwright runs of npm run check:jank -- /kinetic-stagger/ and node tools/draw-size/audit.mjs /kinetic-stagger/.
  • 48 ms wave stagger keeps leading rows ahead while building elastic skew: at t = 120 ms, row 0 (0 ms delay) sits 0.0 px from target while row 4 (192 ms delay) lags 51.2 px behind with 0.013 pre-launch skew; by t = 230 ms, row 4 surges at 0.162 skew and 10.0 px chroma split before all five rows snap to 1:1.
  • Velocity shear and R/B chroma split stay clean inside padded quads: padding each quad by 48 x 36 px avoids clipping sheared card corners and R/B trails (meanDiff = 53.4, maxRB = 223, shearA = 238 vs 0 outside the card at rest).
  • Hit testing survives shuffling and filtering: calling updateElementGeometry() with cached geometryUnit(), toggling data-hit-tick and marking filtered rows inert with an offstage matrix kept moved +1 and Pin clicks landing on the visible rows while skipping filtered rows.
  • Clearing temporary 2D fallback canvases immediately drops removed GPU bytes to zero: setting cv2.width = 0; cv2.height = 0; alongside window.__gfx?.retire?.(cv2) cleared 668 KB of pending 2D fixture memory immediately after Check 5 finished.
